targetPath: /multi-country/brazil_chile_uruguay/interests/food-and-wine/
kind: multi_country_interest
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Explore food-and-wine trips to Brazil, Chile and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  On itineraries combining Brazil, Chile and Uruguay, wine and food experiences are distributed differently. On the Argentina and Patagonia trip, the main tastings take place at Argentine wineries, while Uruguay offers an introduction to Montevideo's cuisine. On the 20-day six-country tour, Chile's Maipo Valley wineries are an optional extra. We compare the stops on both programs and explain which culinary experiences are included and which need separate arrangements.
---

## Brazil, Chile and Uruguay: which food-and-wine itineraries does Ada Tours offer?

Our collection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [26-day journey through Argentina and Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) and a [20-day itinerary through six Latin American countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). Both include [Brazil](/brazil/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Uruguay](/uruguay/) on their main routes, but neither is a standalone trip limited to those three countries.

On our programs, the “Food and Wine” theme applies to the entire itinerary. It **does not mean that tastings are scheduled in each of the three countries**. First compare the actual wine stops:

| Stage of the journey | What is planned |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio or Iguazú, nature and sightseeing excursions, without a dedicated wine route |
| Chile | On the 20-day program, Maipo wineries are offered as an optional excursion |
| Uruguay | One-day introduction to Montevideo; the 26-day itinerary includes a visit to a market with local produce |
| Argentina | On the 26-day itinerary, separate winery days in Mendoza and the Uco Valley |

It is the Argentine section that makes the 26-day option much more wine-focused. Booking it as a tour of Chilean wineries would be a mistake: the main confirmed tasting program is in another country.

## Brazil: Rio and Iguazú instead of a winery tour

The Brazilian parts of these journeys focus on [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and [Iguazú Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The itinerary is oriented toward city sights, tropical forest and waterfalls. Neither route lists vineyard visits, culinary workshops or expert-led tastings in its Brazilian section.

Guests may sample local food during free time and ordinary meals, but that should not be advertised as a separate gastronomic excursion. If your main interest is Brazilian cuisine, markets, culinary traditions or coffee farms, a dedicated program and extra days should be arranged. The [food-and-wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/) section helps identify trips where cuisine and tasting are genuinely important features.

## Chile: Maipo Valley, but only if you select the optional excursion

On the 20-day itinerary, travelers fly from Uruguay to [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). The main program includes a city tour of the capital. An excursion to wineries in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) with a tasting can be added separately; it is a paid extra, not part of the base package.

Maipo is one of Chile's historic winemaking areas. A visit introduces the local vineyards and wine production near Santiago. But booking the excursion affects the capital's schedule: consider its duration and the subsequent flight to Calama, which begins the Atacama stage.

On the 26-day program, Chile is primarily represented by Patagonia and Torres del Paine. No mandatory wine tasting is listed there. The tours therefore answer the question “Will we sample Chilean wine at a winery?” differently: one offers a paid Maipo option, while the other focuses elsewhere.

## Uruguay: Montevideo, its market and local cuisine

On both itineraries, [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is visited from Buenos Aires, with a return to Argentina the same day. The ferry crossing and city sightseeing take up much of the day, leaving little time for an independent extended tasting program.

The 26-day tour explicitly includes a market where travelers can explore local produce and cuisine. The route then continues through urban districts and parks. The 20-day program lists general sightseeing and free time; a specific wine tasting or cooking workshop in Montevideo has not been confirmed.

Uruguay has its own winemaking tradition, but **a visit to a Uruguayan winery is not included on either ready-made itinerary**. If you want a tasting of Uruguayan wine, a visit to a winery and an in-depth look at the country's cuisine, a separate route with additional days is needed. A one-day visit to the capital should not automatically be presented as a full wine tour.

## Where the main wineries of the 26-day program actually are

The most substantial culinary stage of the [26-day Argentina and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) is in Argentina itself. The route visits the Mendoza wine region and also includes Cafayate in the country's northwest.

In the [Luján de Cuyo Valley](/argentina/place/lujan-de-cuyo/), visits to three wineries with tours and tastings are planned. The program covers local grapes, production and wine aging, with lunch at one of the wineries. Another dedicated wine day takes place in the Uco Valley, visiting two more estates. This differs from a single optional stop to sample wine: winemaking occupies several separate stages of the trip.

In addition to the wine regions, the program covers Buenos Aires, both the Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazú, Uruguay, the lake district and Patagonia. Chile is also visited, but the main wine experience remains in Argentina. This distinction should guide travelers for whom winery tastings are a principal reason to travel.

## Comparing the tours: 20 or 26 days

**20 days, six countries.** The route from Rio through Iguazú, Buenos Aires, Montevideo and Santiago continues into Bolivia and Peru. Its strength is its extensive geography and mix of cultures in a limited time. A Maipo winery visit can be added, but several days in Mendoza are not scheduled.

**26 days, Argentina and Patagonia with neighboring countries.** This itinerary gives a deeper experience of Argentina, including full wine-tasting days, together with Patagonia's natural scenery and the main stops in Brazil, Uruguay and Chile. It suits travelers who regard visits to a wine region as a significant reason for the journey.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_vsya_argentina,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026}}

When comparing prices, review paid excursions, flights, meals and tastings separately. The name of a themed collection does not make an optional outing a prepaid service. This applies especially to the Chilean Maipo excursion, which is identified as an extra.

## Planning a trip without losing the wine days

First decide what matters most: a full series of winery visits, exploring local city cuisine or seeing many countries on one journey. For the first option, the route through Mendoza and Uco Valley is the better fit. For the second, Montevideo and free-time stops may be sufficient, with Maipo available as an addition to the 20-day trip.

Consider the route's geography too. Uruguay is visited with a return to Argentina, requiring a second border crossing. Both options include onward journeys or flights between countries with different passport and customs rules. Requirements should be checked by nationality and travel date, particularly when transporting bottles of wine and considering airline baggage restrictions.

Wine days require time for transfers, confirmed tasting reservations and a comfortable pace. It is better to leave breathing room between estates than to cram in too many stops. We can prepare a personalized itinerary with confirmed excursions and suitable logistics.

## Frequently asked questions about food and wine in Brazil, Chile and Uruguay

### Do both tours include Chilean wine tastings?

No. The 20-day program offers a separately paid excursion to [Maipo wineries](/chile/place/maipo-valley/). The main winery visits on the 26-day itinerary take place in Argentina.

### Are Uruguayan wineries included?

No. Uruguay is represented by a [one-day Montevideo visit](/uruguay/place/montevideo/). The 26-day version includes exploring local products at a city market, but not a trip to vineyards.

### Which option is better for wineries?

The [26-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) includes dedicated wine days in Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley. It offers more tastings, although most are in Argentina.

### Can I arrange a gastronomic tour specifically through Brazil, Chile and Uruguay?

Yes, a customized journey with dedicated wineries, markets and culinary excursions can be discussed. It would be a new program with a different duration and price; neither existing route should be marketed as a ready-made specialized tour of only these three countries.

buttonLabel: "Explore nature itineraries through Brazil, Chile and Uruguay"
lead: >-
  On journeys through Brazil, Chile and Uruguay, nature experiences occur in very different regions: Iguazú Falls and tropical forest, glacial Patagonia or the Atacama Desert, followed by Uruguay's coastline and Montevideo. Such trips usually include Argentina as well. Compare the geographical details of each day, rather than just the list of countries.
---

## Nature in Brazil, Chile and Uruguay on one journey

Our collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} featuring Brazil, Chile and Uruguay as main countries. These are multi-day itineraries visiting several natural areas, but their content differs. Some journeys explore Chilean Patagonia, while others visit the Atacama and Bolivia; the Uruguayan section commonly centers on [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/).

**Combining three countries does not mean a tour limited to those three.** The ready-made trips in this collection also visit Argentina, for example, and some continue to Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador and Colombia. Check the nature stops day by day to distinguish excursions from transfers or brief city visits.

To view all themes, open the [Brazil + Chile + Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/brazil_chile_uruguay/). Here, we compare landscape-focused journeys specifically.

## Brazil: Iguazú and the humid Atlantic Forest

[Iguazú Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) is a natural landmark connecting many multi-country itineraries. From the Brazilian side, travelers see a broad panorama of the cascades, while the [Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) offers a different perspective across the river. The two national parks protect valuable sections of the UNESCO-recognized Atlantic Forest.

On a journey from Brazil to Chile through Argentina, Iguazú often provides the first striking natural contrast before the mountains and glaciers. The [17-day four-country trip](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) includes the falls alongside southern Patagonia. On the [20-day six-country program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/), Iguazú precedes the Andes' high-altitude regions.

The humid tropical forest differs sharply from southern Chile's scenery. Before visiting the falls, check which sides are included, how the border crossing is organized and whether there is enough time for trails and viewpoints. Rainfall and river levels can affect access to routes.

## Chile: Patagonia or the Atacama

In southern Chile, the nature program revolves around [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), Puerto Natales, glacial valleys, mountain lakes and Patagonia's open landscapes. The [17-day tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) includes an excursion to Torres del Paine and a visit to Mylodon Cave, after which the journey continues to Argentine glaciers.

The other option is northern Chile. After Santiago, the [20-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) heads to the San Pedro de Atacama region and then to the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) in Bolivia. Here, the main scenery consists of dry mountain valleys, volcanoes and high-altitude terrain. This journey involves different physical demands and some stops at considerable elevation.

The [32-day eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also includes Chile's Atacama, but goes through more countries. It appeals to travelers seeking an extensive introduction to the continent, with frequent changes of location.

These differences are fundamental when planning. Patagonia calls for preparation for wind, variable weather and long road journeys. The Atacama calls for strong sun protection, dry air, cold nights and altitude awareness. Programs in these regions are not interchangeable merely because both count as nature trips in Chile.

## Uruguay: what can you see in a day?

[Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) stands on the shores of the Río de la Plata. Its long Rambla promenade, city parks and views of the water offer a peaceful interlude on a busy journey. On several combined tours, Uruguay features a group sightseeing tour of the capital, followed by a return across the Río de la Plata to Buenos Aires.

Uruguay's natural attractions extend well beyond its city waterfront, including Atlantic beaches, dunes, coastal lagoons and protected areas. For a separate journey, [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) or the eastern coastline can be considered. But these stops **should not automatically be included in the description of a tour for sale** unless they appear on its actual itinerary.

This is the main feature of the combination: Chilean and Brazilian nature stages can occupy several days, while the Uruguayan stage may be cultural and urban. The [Uruguay overview](/uruguay/) helps explain which nature additions would require more time.

## How four types of itinerary differ

| Natural focus | Example route |
|---|---|
| Patagonia and Iguazú | [17 days, four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) |
| Atacama and Uyuni | [20 days, six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) |
| Extensive overview of the continent | [32 days, eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) |
| Glaciers and lakes | [26 days through Argentina and Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) |

First decide whether glaciers or a high-altitude desert interest you more. Then compare journeys by duration and the actual excursion days. For a trip centered on nature, the number of hours genuinely spent at each site usually matters more than the number of countries.

Flights and international crossings can take a considerable share of a longer journey. Visiting Iguazú and Patagonia requires dividing time between distant regions. The Atacama and Uyuni demand altitude awareness and lengthy overland travel. Uruguay is often more conveniently included via Argentina than connected directly with southern Chile.

## Weather and travel preparation

The main climate contrasts on these routes are warm, humid Brazil, cold and windy southern Patagonia or Chile's dry highlands, and milder coastal Uruguay. No single seasonal recommendation works for the entire combination.

For Iguazú, bring protection for electronics against water and comfortable shoes. Patagonia requires windproof and warm layers; the Atacama calls for sun protection and clothing for cold nights. Before traveling, check national park restrictions and conditions on individual walking trails.

Ada Tours helps select the sequence of countries and coordinate flights, ferries, local excursions and accommodation. Inclusion of a particular service is confirmed by the chosen program; VIP status or a private format should not be inferred from the catalog title alone.

## Frequently asked questions about journeys through Brazil, Chile and Uruguay

### Do these programs visit only three countries?

No. Many also include Argentina, while longer journeys may continue into Bolivia and Peru. The exact countries are listed on each tour page.

### Can I see Iguazú and Torres del Paine on one journey?

Yes. Such combinations exist, including the 17-day four-country program. Time allocated to both nature regions and the flights between them are important.

### What is more interesting for nature in Chile: the Atacama or Patagonia?

The Atacama offers desert and high-altitude scenery, while Patagonia is known for glaciers, mountain lakes and southern parks. They are different kinds of trip with different demands.

### Are Uruguay's natural parks included?

On most of the longer itineraries described, Uruguay is primarily an urban stage. Check the specific program or arrange an extra stop for a separate nature excursion.

### When should I choose dates for the journey?

After deciding on the main nature destination. Conditions at Iguazú, Patagonia and the Atacama differ too much to rely on one season for all three areas.

lead: >-
  The wildlife collection for Brazil, Chile and Uruguay features a 32-day journey through eight countries. The included opportunities to observe birds and marine animals take place in Ecuador's Galápagos Islands. Iguazú and the Atacama provide scenery, while Montevideo is a city visit. We also compare this itinerary with nature routes through Patagonia and the Bolivian highlands, where visiting a park alone does not mean a dedicated wildlife-watching excursion.

## Watching wildlife on a journey through Brazil, Chile and Uruguay

Our collection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: a [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Brazil, Chile and Uruguay are among its main countries, but the dedicated wildlife activities take place on an additional Ecuadorian stage. **Natural landscapes and wildlife observation are different themes:** Iguazú and the Atacama alone do not make an itinerary a wildlife tour. Uruguay is represented by [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) and a ferry across the Río de la Plata. For comparison, we also discuss scenic itineraries from the [nature collection for these countries](/multi-country/brazil_chile_uruguay/interests/nature/).

This distinction is essential if seeing animals is the reason for your journey. Visiting waterfalls, walking in a national park and deliberately watching wildlife are different activities. A nature tag on the entire trip does not guarantee a safari or a sighting of a rare species in each of the three countries.

For general geography and other formats, explore [Brazil, Chile and Uruguay tours](/multi-country/brazil_chile_uruguay/). Here, we consider **which natural areas are actually on the itinerary, how much time is allocated to them and what sightings are realistic**.

## Brazil: Iguazú and the Atlantic Forest

A shared nature stop is [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The falls are surrounded by subtropical Atlantic Forest, with ecosystems protected on both sides of the Brazil–Argentina border. Different bird species, monkeys, tapirs and large predators live in the region, but seeing a particular animal on the standard viewpoint paths is not a promised part of the excursion.

**The waterfalls themselves are the main attraction**: huge clouds of spray, river views and forested slopes. Waterproof protection will help your camera, and nonslip soles are useful for walking. Paths can be wet after rain, and spray may affect visibility close to the cascades.

An excursion to the [Bird Park near Iguazú](/brazil/place/parque-das-aves/) may be added to some programs. This is different from searching for birds in the wild; viewing conditions and availability depend on the chosen visit format. Another possible extra is the “Macuco Safari” boat outing, where proximity to the falls and the likelihood of getting wet matter more than any promise of seeing wild animals.

On the [17-day trip through Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Uruguay](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/), Iguazú follows the Patagonia stage and Buenos Aires. On the [20-day six-country program](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), the falls come on the route from Rio into Argentina. This is a nature day within a long itinerary, not a multi-day tropical forest expedition.

## Chile: two fundamentally different nature programs

**Patagonia suits travelers who want mountain landscapes and a chance of seeing animals in open terrain.** The [17-day four-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) begins in Santiago, then goes to [Puerto Natales and Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/), crossing into Argentina toward El Calafate afterward. On the [26-day journey through Argentina and Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), the Chilean section also features Patagonian landscapes, with considerable time devoted to Argentine regions.

In Torres del Paine, open steppe meets lakes, forests and mountain ranges. Guanacos and birds can be seen under suitable circumstances. **Sightings are possible, but the tour is not the same as a booked safari excursion:** animals roam freely, and the outcome depends on weather, timing and chance. Patagonia's wind and rapid changes in weather call for windproof and waterproof clothing even during the warmer season.

On other journeys, the Chilean stage runs through [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) toward the Bolivian border. On the [20-day route from Rio to Machu Picchu](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) and the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), this marks the transition from cities and waterfalls into high-altitude desert landscapes. Dry air, intense sun and cool nights are more relevant here than forest wildlife. The high-altitude lagoons where flamingos may be seen are mostly **on the Bolivian section** of these itineraries, not within Chile.

| Chilean stage | Main experience |
|---|---|
| Torres del Paine | Mountains, steppe and lakes; possible guanaco sightings |
| Atacama | Desert, altitude and the transition to Bolivia |

If your goal is to spend more time among Patagonian landscapes, compare the 17- and 26-day programs. If you want contrasting natural zones across the continent, the longer journeys through the Atacama, Bolivia and Peru may be more suitable.

## Uruguay: the real nature of the visit

On our journeys, [Uruguay](/uruguay/) is mainly included via Montevideo. The 20- and 32-day programs, for example, include a day trip from Buenos Aires across the Río de la Plata, with a city tour. This offers views of the estuary and the waterfront of another South American capital, but **not a dedicated wildlife program in Uruguay**.

This distinction helps you choose according to your actual interest. If you want to watch birds in Uruguay's wetlands or explore protected coastal areas, these stops need to be explicitly included in a separately agreed itinerary. The Brazil + Chile + Uruguay catalog alone does not promise them.

## The wildlife itinerary and three scenic alternatives

The list of three filtered countries is not enough. Of the four programs compared here, only the 32-day journey belongs in this wildlife collection. The other three are nature tours: scenery and possible chance encounters do not replace an included wildlife-watching activity.

- [17 days: Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Uruguay](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) — a more focused route through Torres del Paine, [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) and Iguazú.
- [26 days: Argentina and Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) — a detailed exploration of several Argentine regions, including Patagonia, with the other three countries on the route.
- [20 days: six countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) — a contrast between Iguazú's Atlantic Forest, the Atacama and Bolivia's highlands. Patagonia's national park is not part of this itinerary.
- [32 days: eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) — an expanded journey that adds the Galápagos Islands **in Ecuador** to Iguazú and the Atacama. Included opportunities to see birds, iguanas and sea lions on the island excursion day are what make this a wildlife tour. This stage must not be attributed to Chile or Uruguay.

All four itineraries include some of the same countries but are hardly interchangeable in how they explore nature. Some tours visit both sides of Iguazú; crossing the Brazil–Argentina border still requires specific preparation for documents and timing.

## Seasons, weather and travel arrangements

The most striking contrast is between the warm, humid forest around Iguazú, cool and windy Patagonia, and the dry Atacama highlands. Even if a journey takes place during spring or summer in the Southern Hemisphere, a single set of lightweight clothes will not suit the climatic conditions of every stage.

For Patagonia, pack layers, wind and rain protection and comfortable shoes for unpaved paths. For Iguazú, bring light quick-drying clothes and waterproof protection for devices. For the Atacama, take a hat, sun protection, a warm evening layer and prepare for gradual acclimatization before the onward journey into Bolivia.

On longer programs, the journey through Bolivia can reach very high elevations. Altitude affects even physically fit travelers, so discuss the pace of ascent, rest and medical contraindications in advance. The 17-day Patagonia itinerary presents different challenges: weather may alter road conditions, while wind can affect the duration of stops.

We help coordinate the sequence of countries, flight connections and overland stages, allowing realistic time between excursions. Entry requirements for **every country on the actual route** are checked separately for each traveler's citizenship and documents, including Argentina or Bolivia where applicable. These countries have different currencies and payment systems; acceptance of Russian or foreign cards, exchange options and cash use must be confirmed for the individual trip without promising a universal payment method.

## Frequently asked questions about nature tours through Brazil, Chile and Uruguay

### Can I see animals in all three countries?

The collection does not promise separate wildlife-watching activities in all three. The included wildlife stage of the 32-day tour takes place in the Galápagos in Ecuador; Iguazú and the Atacama focus on landscapes, and Uruguay on Montevideo. Sightings of particular species depend on natural conditions.

### Is there an itinerary including Patagonia and Iguazú?

Yes. The [17-day four-country tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-uruguay/) combines these natural areas. Consider the overland crossing between Chile and Argentina, Patagonia's weather and the onward flights.

### Is flamingo-watching included in Chile?

On the longer itineraries, lagoons with flamingos may be part of the Bolivian section after the Atacama. Check the exact days instead of assuming all high-altitude lagoons belong to Chile.

### How does this collection differ from Brazil-only trips?

The nature program here spans several ecosystems but requires more travel. For more time exploring the tropical forest and waterfalls, compare [nature tours of Brazil](/interests/nature/tours/brazil/) and specific programs featuring Iguazú.

### Which tour should I choose for wildlife rather than a large country count?

For included wildlife observations, consider the Galápagos stage of the 32-day tour in Ecuador. Compare Torres del Paine, Perito Moreno and Iguazú primarily for landscapes; a chance sighting is not a dedicated wildlife excursion. Then check the number of overnight stays, excursion types and time available for observations. The longest program does not necessarily give you more time in each natural area.

lead: >-
  Brazil and Colombia are combined in Ada Tours' current 32-day journey through eight South American countries. The trip begins in São Paulo, Rio and at Iguazú Falls and concludes in Medellín, Guatapé, Cartagena and Bogotá. Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador lie between the two countries on the itinerary. Here we explain the journey's duration and how to prepare for different climates, documents, flights and expenses.
---

## Brazil and Colombia on one tour: how the journey really works

**Our “Brazil + Colombia” selection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}.** This is not a short itinerary flying directly from Rio to Bogotá, but an [extensive 32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). It begins in Brazil on October 22, 2026, and concludes in Colombia in November. Between these stages, travelers explore six other countries, including high-altitude Bolivia and the Galápagos Islands.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

There is an easily overlooked detail when choosing a route by country names: **almost three weeks of travel and excursions separate the Brazilian and Colombian stages**. If you want only Rio and Cartagena over 10–12 days, the published 32-day tour should not be treated as a ready-made two-country option. Ada Tours can discuss a different sequence and duration for a personalized journey, but the services of any new offer are agreed separately.

| Part of the route | When it occurs |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Days 1–6 |
| Argentina – Ecuador | Days 7–25 |
| Colombia | Days 26–32 |

The last day includes a flight from Bogotá to São Paulo for an onward connection home. This matters for passports, possible re-entry into Brazil and airline bookings: the end of Colombia's excursion program is not the end of the entire travel sequence.

## Starting in Brazil: from Rio to Iguazú Falls

The journey begins in [São Paulo](/brazil/place/sao-paulo/) and continues to [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Two days of sightseeing in Rio cover Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain and the city center. This sequence allows travelers to see the architecture and oceanfront before moving on to the nature portion.

On day five, the group travels to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Day six focuses on the Brazilian side of the falls: panoramic viewpoints, tropical scenery and walks overlooking the cascades. The following day, travelers cross the border to visit the Argentine side of Iguazú and then continue toward Buenos Aires. **This is a full international border crossing, not a walk within a single national park.** Visiting both sides requires checking documents, entry arrangements and tickets for each country.

The waterfalls are particularly relevant for weather preparation. Iguazú is warm and humid, and spray can soak clothes at the viewpoints. Nonslip footwear, waterproof protection for equipment and light quick-drying clothing are advisable. The same light clothes will later be useful in hot Cartagena, but the Andes call for entirely different layers.

## Finishing in Colombia: Andes, Guatapé and the Caribbean Sea

After the Galápagos Islands and an overnight stay in Guayaquil, the group reaches [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) on day 26. The following day includes an outing to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñón rock. A Medellín city tour, including Comuna 13, follows before a flight to the coast.

[Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) has its own sightseeing day: the historic center, fortifications, squares and streets of the Old Town. Here the route reaches the Caribbean Sea. The next stages include a flight to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), city sightseeing and an outing to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and its Salt Cathedral.

These represent three markedly different climatic regions within Colombia alone. Medellín is in a mountain valley; Cartagena is hot and humid; Bogotá lies high in the Andes, with noticeably cooler evenings. When packing, do not rely on the word “tropics” or expect one lightweight outfit to suffice for all seven Colombian days.

### What is included in the published itinerary

The 32-day tour includes 4-star hotel accommodation, domestic flights, scheduled transfers with a driver, specified admission tickets and guided excursions. Guiding languages differ: for example, Russian-speaking guides are listed in Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá, while English-speaking guides accompany the Guatapé and Zipaquirá excursions.

International flights to the start of the journey and back home, additional excursions, meals beyond those specified, gratuities and laundry are excluded. These details matter more than a promotional “turnkey tour” label: compare prices by what the services actually include. The [full program and conditions](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) are on the tour page; this article examines the particular challenges of connecting the countries.

## Flights and borders: why the route cannot be shortened by looking at a map

Brazil and Colombia share a border in the Amazon region, but **that does not make overland travel between Rio and Bogotá a simple tourist option**. The key cities are far from that border. When traveling between major urban areas, available aviation hubs, possible connections and arrival airports matter much more than straight-line distance.

The published tour follows a different chain: Brazil → Argentina → Uruguay → Chile → Bolivia → Peru → Ecuador → Colombia. It includes the border crossing at Iguazú, a high-altitude road section from Chile into Bolivia and the flight to the Galápagos. Some days combine an excursion with an onward flight, so a delayed departure may affect meeting a guide, checking into a hotel or visiting a planned site.

Ada Tours helps review the sequence of stages, realistic flight connections and adequate buffer time. For international segments purchased independently, check whether flights are on one or separate tickets, baggage allowances and whether another check-in is required during a connection. If the arrival and onward airports differ, calculate the ground-transfer time separately.

## Travel documents: visa-free entry still requires border preparation

**For a tourist with an ordinary Russian international passport, Brazil permits short visa-free visits of up to 90 days within any 180-day period.** The Brazilian Embassy in Moscow explains this arrangement. Employment, study and other purposes have different rules. For this itinerary, consider both the **first entry** and a possible return via São Paulo on the journey home.

Colombian consular rules include Russia among nationalities exempt from visas for short visits. The normal initial authorized stay is determined by immigration control under current regulations. The absence of a visa sticker does not remove checks on passport validity, return or onward tickets, purpose of travel and immigration forms.

The 32-day itinerary includes six more countries besides these two. Different citizenship, dual nationality or transit through a third country may significantly alter the requirements. A useful preparation sequence is:

1. List **every actual entry**, including the Argentine side of Iguazú and the return connection in Brazil.
2. Check passport, visa and health-document requirements for each nationality and every country of transit.
3. Match airline reservations, passport names, arrival and departure dates, connection rules and possible re-entry conditions.
4. Check Colombia's immigration forms, including Check-Mig, and the carrier's requirements immediately before travel.

Entry regimes may change. This guidance for Russian citizens was checked against official materials on **October 16, 2026**; the final arrangements for other nationalities must be determined separately.

## Reais and pesos: payments at the beginning and end of the trip

The Brazilian real (BRL) and Colombian peso (COP) are separate currencies. US dollars may be useful as a reserve for an international trip, but that does not mean every café, museum or taxi will accept them directly. Local money is generally more convenient for small purchases. Before exchanging, consider the rate, commission and amount actually received, not merely a “USD” sign on a price tag.

Do not confuse Colombian pesos with Argentine or Chilean pesos; their exchange rates and circulation rules differ. Ecuador, visited between Brazil and Colombia on this itinerary, uses the US dollar. For the journey as a whole, it makes sense to separate money for tour payments, everyday personal expenses and a reserve for situations where electronic payments are unavailable.

**Russian-issued bank cards should not be assumed to work universally abroad.** Check each card and network with its issuing bank and for the relevant countries. Ada Tours helps list expected payments and review local payment options, but cannot guarantee that a particular bank's card will work or promise currency exchange services of its own.

## October and November: packing and health considerations

The Brazilian stage falls in late October. Rio and Iguazú call for clothing suitable for warm and sometimes humid weather. Toward the end of the trip, in November, travelers move through mountain-valley Medellín, hot Cartagena and cooler high-altitude Bogotá. Between them are the highlands of Chile, Bolivia and Peru, as well as the Galápagos. Layers are therefore more practical than packing a separate “summer” suitcase.

Useful basics include a light windproof jacket, warm layer for the Andes, breathable clothes for humid cities, reliable shoes, sun and rain protection. Check cabin and checked baggage limits for domestic flights separately; they may differ from the international ticket.

Health preparation depends on the actual route. In 2026, Colombia's Ministry of Health warned of yellow-fever risks in certain municipalities and recommended advance vaccination before traveling to high-risk areas. This **does not mean** every district of Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena has the same requirements, or that every traveler must show a certificate. Confirm the exact areas, transit route and current rules, and discuss vaccination with a doctor in light of contraindications.

If the journey includes Bolivia's high-altitude section, consider the risk of altitude sickness. The published itinerary includes a stay in San Pedro de Atacama before the jeep route, but that does not guarantee an absence of symptoms. Discuss chronic medical conditions or concerns about altitude tolerance in advance; travel insurance should cover every country and activity on the actual route.

## Who this combination suits and what to ask before booking

The longer route suits travelers who want to see very different regions of South America on one holiday and are comfortable with frequent hotel changes, flights and altitude. It is less suited to people wanting a relaxed two weeks exclusively on the beaches of Brazil and Colombia: that request calls for a separate itinerary with fewer transfers.

Before deciding, compare dates, physical demands, guiding languages, included tickets, flight arrangements, personal expenses and medical considerations. The [multi-country tours page](/multi-country/) offers other geographical combinations; for a shorter Brazilian trip see [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/), and for a Colombian one see [Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/). These are distinct choices, not three names for the same product.

The Brazilian section covers days 1–6, while the Colombian stage begins on day 26. These are two parts of one continuous 32-day itinerary, with Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador between them.

For ordinary tourist visits, Russian citizens benefit from the applicable visa-free arrangements in Brazil and Colombia, but each country determines permitted stays, purposes and border formalities separately. No. Brazil uses reais, Colombia uses Colombian pesos. USD may form part of your cash reserve, but US dollars or an international bank card do not guarantee payment everywhere.

## Adventures in Brazil and Colombia: what the current itinerary includes

Between [Brazil](/brazil/) and [Colombia](/colombia/), travelers encounter widely differing landscapes. The Brazilian days begin in Rio de Janeiro and continue to Iguazú Falls. The Colombian days conclude the extensive route with Medellín, an excursion to Guatapé and sightseeing in Cartagena and Bogotá.

Our collection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. It currently centers on [“8 South American Countries in 32 Days”](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The tour has an Adventure tag, but the tag describes the whole program. Between Brazil and Colombia, travelers visit Argentina, Uruguay, Chile, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. This product does not promise a direct two-country journey through Brazil and Colombia.

| Stage | What is actually planned |
|---|---|
| Rio de Janeiro | Corcovado, Christ the Redeemer, Sugarloaf Mountain, sightseeing |
| Iguazú | Waterfalls and national park; optional Macuco Safari boat trip |
| Medellín and Guatapé | El Peñón rock, the town of Guatapé and reservoir |
| Cartagena and Bogotá | Historic districts, Monserrate and Salt Cathedral |

## Iguazú: close to the water and inside a nature park

In Brazil, the journey begins with arrival in São Paulo, followed by two sightseeing days in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The group visits Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado and rides a cable car to Sugarloaf via Urca Hill. These are busy city excursions where comfortable walking is more important than sporting ability.

Next the group flies to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). The Brazilian side of the falls is visited on a group excursion with a Russian-speaking guide. The viewpoints reveal the cascades and surrounding tropical forest. Iguazú National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its natural value.

For a closer experience of the river, the tour offers **Macuco Safari for an additional $130 per person**. This includes a guided drive along a forest road, a short walk and a motorboat ride toward the falls. The Bird Park is also optional, at $50 per person. These services must not be presented as included in the base tour price. Boat operations depend on water levels and the operator; availability is confirmed for the visit date.

Technical rafting, bungee jumping and expedition-style whitewater trips are not listed in the Brazilian days. Here, the adventure interest is primarily expressed through a major natural attraction and the possibility of a separately booked active excursion.

## Guatapé and El Peñón rock: Colombia's nature stop

After traveling through other countries, guests reach [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/). The following day features an eight-hour excursion with an English-speaking guide to [El Peñón de Guatapé rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/).

The program includes a stop at a replica of old El Peñol, an introduction to the rocky monolith, a town known for its colorful raised decorations on house facades, and the surrounding reservoirs. A local mototaxi may be used during the visit. The scenery differs sharply from Iguazú: instead of waterfalls and humid forest, travelers see mountains, stretches of water and the colorful facades of a small Colombian town.

El Peñón is famous for its long staircase leading to upper viewpoints. However, **the climb itself, the admission ticket and access to the stairs are not specified as mandatory prepaid services** in the selected program. Anyone traveling specifically to reach the top should confirm these conditions separately, including physical demands and whether the stairs are open.

The day also includes walks and photo stops. It is best described as an active sightseeing and nature excursion, rather than a multi-day trek in the Colombian Andes.

## Medellín, Comuna 13 and onward travel to Cartagena

The next day covers Medellín and [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/), followed by a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/). Comuna 13 is known for its history of urban transformation and street art. Visiting it complements the Guatapé outing with insights into city life, contemporary culture and public spaces.

In Cartagena, sightseeing includes fortifications and historic neighborhoods: San Felipe de Barajas Fortress, old streets, squares and the coastal bay. This stage is best suited to people who enjoy history and walking. It includes no advertised jungle treks, river rafting or specialist water sports.

For alternative routes within the country, explore [all Colombia tours](/colombia/tour/) or [cultural journeys through Latin America](/interests/culture-and-history/). Colombia offers several types of travel, so when choosing an adventure product, check the specific activities and hours rather than just the theme tag.

## Where the more demanding outings occur on the 32-day journey

The complete itinerary earns its Adventure tag for other reasons as well. In Chile, the group travels to San Pedro de Atacama, after which the Bolivian section includes a two-day 4×4 trip across high-altitude lagoons and salt flats. These days involve altitude, remote roads and changing weather. The Bolivia stage also includes La Paz, Tiwanaku, Uyuni and the transfer toward Peru's border.

The route then visits Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu, followed by the Galápagos Islands. This whole sequence explains the adventure theme. Brazil and Colombia themselves offer a gentler version: walking, natural panoramas and day excursions.

This is an important distinction. If you are choosing the two countries for demanding treks, sporting rafting or multi-day routes through remote parts of Colombia, the current product would need to be redesigned. If you are ready for a 32-day exploration of the continent, the contrasts between Iguazú, mountain passes and Guatapé become an advantage.

## Logistics and physical demands

The Brazilian leg includes a domestic flight between Rio and Iguazú and sightseeing transfers. In Colombia, the route arrives in Medellín, then flies to Cartagena and on to Bogotá. Brazil and Colombia occur at opposite ends of the 32-day program, with many flights and overnight stops in other countries between them.

The tour price includes domestic flights, main transfers, four-star hotels, specified excursions and meals. International flights, optional excursions, personal expenses and tips are excluded. It is important to distinguish the overall tour price from the cost of individual activities: the Iguazú boat outing and other optional excursions are charged separately.

The climate changes several times: humid Rio, the falls, dry Atacama, cold high-altitude regions and Caribbean Cartagena. Excursion days call for comfortable shoes and protection from sun and rain. Bolivia requires warm clothing and an assessment of altitude tolerance. Consult a doctor about high-altitude travel in advance, particularly if you have cardiovascular or respiratory conditions.

The journey crosses eight countries. Visa and border requirements, transit rules, passport validity, safety advice and insurance must be reviewed for each nationality and set of dates. High-risk regions of Colombia cannot be assumed to be part of the usual tourist itinerary just because the country appears in the name.

## Deciding whether this tour suits you

Choose this program if you want to combine South America's natural landmarks with urban history and are prepared for a lengthy journey. The principal natural attractions in Brazil are Iguazú and Tijuca Forest, while Colombia offers El Peñón and the Guatapé reservoir. The more demanding road and high-altitude stages are concentrated in other countries.

If you have less time, consider a dedicated customized two-country trip; the program, domestic flights and required overnight stays would differ. Ada Tours helps match desired activities to actual days, duration and included services.
